rubric.result:
Four sentences of `### Desired end state`, each measured against the sum of the diff. (1) "`server/src/analysis/coupling.ts` exports `AnalyzeCoupling`, a class whose `run` reads the same window/main-folder/path scope as `heatTree` and answers the coupled pairs of that level's children, each with its co-change count and percent": the new module declares `export class AnalyzeCoupling` whose `run` resolves the scope with heat.ts's own `resolveMainFolder`/`normalizePath`/`buildGrid`/`bucketIndex`/`countTouching`/`isWithin`/`touchedChildren` (imported, not re-derived) and returns `pairs` carrying `coChanges` and `percent` per pair. (2) "`GET /api/repos/:id/coupling?window=&path=` answers that payload, cached by HEAD sha exactly like `/heat`, with no author name or email anywhere in it": `router.get('/repos/:id/coupling', ...)` in routes.ts reads the same six inputs as the `/heat` handler above it, remembers through its own `createCache(CACHE_LIMIT)` with the same `keyOf([repo, window, headSha, dayOf(now), mainFolder, path])` and the same `(value) => value.headSha === headSha` guard, and answers `{ window, ...coupling }`; the `Coupling` shape carries only mainFolder/fallback/path/commits/minCoOccurrences/headSha/pairs, and the pair fields are child names, kinds and counts, so no author identity travels (coupling.test.ts's fourth test pins that over the serialized payload). The port widening in app.ts is what makes the handler reachable. (3) "`HeatBlock` fetches coupling right after heat resolves a level, at `heat.path`, and draws an \"Acoplamiento\" section below the existing rows: one row per pair above the minimum, sorted from most to least coupled, and a clear message (naming the minimum) when the window has none": the second `useEffect` of Heat.tsx returns early while `heat === null` and then calls `fetchCoupling(repoId, window, heat?.path, signal)`; the render adds `

Acoplamiento

` immediately after the heat footer, one `data-testid="coupling-row"` div per `couplingRows(coupling.pairs)` entry, and `noCouplingHeadline(coupling.minCoOccurrences)` when that list is empty — the minimum is read off the payload, so the message names it. The filtering (`coChanges < MIN_CO_OCCURRENCES` dropped) and the ordering (`percent` desc, then `coChanges` desc, then `a`) are produced in `pairsOf` and the block draws them in arrival order, which is what "sorted from most to least coupled" resolves to end to end. (4) "Changing the window, or drilling into another folder, recomputes coupling exactly like Calor's existing heat": the effect's dependency array is `[repoId, window, heat?.path]`, and a window change nulls `heat` first, so `heat?.path` transitions through `undefined` and the coupling fetch fires again for the newly resolved level; a drill-down changes `heat.path` directly. Every promise exists somewhere in the accumulated diff, and none of them is produced by an earlier commit and undone by a later one.

`## Commits` lists twelve commits: the eight task commits (1/8 to 8/8) and four bookkeeping commits. I read what each of the four touches in the accumulated diff rather than taking the characterisation on trust: the only non-task paths in `## Files changed` are `docs/superpowers/metrics/issue-51.jsonl` (new, run telemetry), the plan itself, and the eight task verdicts. Inside the plan's hunks the whole change is three `**Files:**` additions (Task 3 gains `server/src/analysis/index.test.ts`; Task 4 gains `server/src/api/errors.test.ts` with the paragraph explaining why widening the `Pick` forces `couplingOf: fail` there; Task 8 gains `web/src/App.test.tsx` with the paragraph explaining the `stubApi` gap) plus §8's clean-tree predicate gaining the two `':!.agent/run-51...'` exclusions. Not one of them touches production code, a test, or a file another task's `**Files:**` line claims, so none is a task reversing or contradicting another task; they are plan and process bookkeeping, outside the per-task objective framework, like the plan document and its §8. Among the eight task commits the chain is strictly additive and each one leaves the previous standing: Task 1 exports heat.ts's five decisions and routes `childrenOf` through the extracted `touchedChildren`; Task 2 consumes exactly those five by import; Task 3 wires `couplingOf` into the barrel beside `heatTree`; Task 4 widens `AnalysisPort` and adds the route; Task 5 declares the payload in `web/` and adds `fetchCoupling`; Task 6 adds `couplingRows`/`COUPLING_ROW_LIMIT` and the two copy functions; Task 7 adds the fetch effect and the `/coupling` branch of `stubHeat`; Task 8 renders and widens that same double with a `pairs` parameter (default `[]`, so every earlier call site answers what it answered before). No reversal anywhere: no export added by an earlier task is removed later, no cap or threshold is redefined, and the one rename (Task 7's `emptyCouplingOf` to Task 8's `couplingOf(level, pairs)`) widens the helper Task 7 created instead of replacing it with a second wording. No scaffolding for an intermediate state survives. One real defect does live in the relationship between two tasks and is reported below: Task 6 produces `CouplingRow.barWidth` for the section Task 8 draws, and Task 8's section draws no bar. Each task's own judge saw it and left it, in each case because it was outside the one task it could see.

`## Señal` reads `(sin señal declarada — el issue no trae la sección "## Señal de observabilidad"; el juez de slice mide su ítem observabilidad como sin-vara)`. It opens with `(sin señal declarada`, so no signal was ever declared for this slice and there is nothing to measure the accumulated diff against: the three checks (production code emits it, with the repo's own instrumentation, every label bounded) and the redundancy smell all need a declared signal as their subject. `simplicity.md`'s "Observability answers to a reader who exists" is the rule this item would have measured with, and it stays unused. Not `no-aplica`: this is not a reasoned `N/A — <razón>` exemption a human approved, it is the absence of the yardstick itself, which is the normal state of an epic groomed before the `Señal` column existed.

findings.what:
Task 6 computes a bar width for every coupling row and Task 8's row never draws it, so the field crosses from `heat-rows.ts` into `Heat.tsx` with no reader. `couplingRows` returns `CouplingRow` = `CouplingPair` + `barWidth`, and its own test pins the three widths ('100.0%', '90.0%', '2.5%'); the render Task 8 wrote is `
{row.a} ↔ {row.b} · {row.percent}%
` — text only, no bar span, unlike the heat rows above it, which draw theirs through `rowCells(row)`. So `barWidth` is computed on every render of the section and never reaches the DOM. The case that shows it: change the expression to `'0.0%'` and no test of the slice fails except `heat-rows.test.ts`'s own, which is the producer testing itself; nothing on screen moves. Task 6's objective ('the row shaping (bar width) ... exist as pure, tested functions') is honoured and Task 8's objective ('draws one row per pair above the minimum, sorted, and a clear message when there is none') is honoured too — each was written as if the other side of the field existed, and the plan is what split them that way (§3 names `heatRows` as 'the bar-width math the new `couplingRows` copies', while Task 8's `Call site` block prescribes a row with no bar). `estado-final` is unaffected: `### Desired end state` promises 'one row per pair above the minimum, sorted', never a bar, so the slice delivers what it promised. Both per-task judges declared this and declined it as out of their reach (Task 6: 'the four new exports have no caller in the tree today, and the caller is named in the desired end state'; Task 8: '`CouplingRow.barWidth` stays unread by the new row, but that field arrived in an earlier task's `heat-rows.ts` and this diff does not touch that file'), so it is counted once, here. `medium`: the slice is right as delivered, and whoever reviews the pull request picks one of the two repairs — draw the bar in the coupling row, or drop `barWidth` and let `couplingRows` return the capped pairs.
findings.evidence: `export interface CouplingRow extends CouplingPair { /** CSS width of the bar, relative to the most coupled pair of the level */ barWidth: string }` — against `conventions/simplicity.md`: "A field crossing a layer with no consumer at the other end." and "The question: **which call breaks without it?** Name it. If none does, it goes."
